nodes.content: Develop expressive speech synthesis that transfers phrase-level emotion across speakers while preserving speaker identity and independently specified emphasis.
requirements: Listeners identify intended emotion in ≥80% of phrases, including emotion–emphasis combinations absent from training.
Emphasis placement accuracy exceeds 90%, with listener-rated speaker similarity no worse than neutral synthesis.

nodes.content: Train compositional diffusion TTS with contrastively anchored speaker timbre, transferable phrase-emotion tokens, and independently controlled word-emphasis masks.
Does separating phrase-emotion tokens from word-emphasis masks preserve emotion recognition on unseen combinations without degrading target-speaker similarity?
Disentangled conditioning achieves ≥80% emotion recognition and >90% emphasis accuracy on withheld emotion–emphasis combinations, with speaker-similarity MOS ≥ neutral.
On EmoEmph-Split’s 12 withheld combinations, collect 100 listeners’ emotion labels, emphasis choices, and speaker-similarity MOS versus neutral.
EmoEmph-Split’s 12 withheld combinations yielded 84% emotion recognition, 93% emphasis accuracy, and speaker-similarity MOS 4.1/5 versus neutral 4.0/5.
Retain disentangled conditioning: withheld-combination recognition and emphasis exceed targets, while speaker-similarity MOS remains above neutral.
Using the retained architecture, expand EmoEmph-Split to unseen speakers and benchmark emotion recognition, emphasis placement, and neutral-relative similarity.
Add 20 unseen speakers to EmoEmph-Split v2; collect blinded emotion, emphasis, and neutral-relative speaker-similarity ratings.
EmoEmph-Split v2 benchmark: synthesized phrases from 20 unseen speakers, withheld emotion–emphasis combinations, and blinded listener ratings.
Bootstrap EmoEmph-Split v2’s per-speaker ratings against 80% emotion, >90% emphasis, and neutral speaker-similarity thresholds.
EmoEmph-Split v2: 20 unseen speakers, withheld combinations; 82% emotion recognition, 92% emphasis accuracy, speaker-similarity MOS 4.0 versus neutral 3.9.
Adopt compositional diffusion TTS for cross-speaker transfer: withheld-combination scores meet targets, and speaker-similarity MOS exceeds neutral.
A joint prosody code lowers withheld-combination emotion recognition below 80% versus separated controls’ 82%, without improving speaker-similarity MOS.
Compare parameter-matched joint-prosody and separated-control TTS on EmoEmph-Split v2’s withheld combinations, measuring emotion recognition and speaker-similarity MOS.
On EmoEmph-Split v2, joint-prosody achieved 83% emotion recognition versus separated 82%, and speaker-similarity MOS 4.1 versus 4.0.
Compute speaker-stratified bootstrap intervals for joint-minus-separated emotion recognition and speaker-similarity MOS on EmoEmph-Split v2.
Equal-speaker bootstrap: joint emotion recognition was 78% versus separated 82% (difference 95% CI: −8 to −1 points); MOS difference −0.1.
Train speaker-adversarial emotion adapters and duration-constrained emphasis controllers over a frozen TTS backbone with preserved speaker embeddings.
On unseen speakers, do duration-constrained emphasis controllers disrupt emotion cues despite speaker-adversarial adapters preserving timbre?
On EmoEmph-Split v2’s unseen speakers, duration-constrained adapters retain ≥80% emotion recognition, >90% emphasis accuracy, and speaker-similarity MOS ≥ neutral.
Benchmark duration-constrained adapters on EmoEmph-Split v2’s withheld combinations across 20 unseen speakers: emotion recognition, emphasis accuracy, and neutral-relative similarity MOS.
EmoEmph-Split v2 adapters achieved 81% emotion recognition, 94% emphasis accuracy, and speaker-similarity MOS 4.1 versus neutral 4.0.
Following adapters’ 81% recognition, ablate duration constraints on unseen speakers; compare emotion confusions, emphasis accuracy, and speaker-similarity MOS.
Synthesize matched EmoEmph-Split v2 phrases with duration constraints enabled or disabled; collect blinded emotion, emphasis, and speaker-similarity judgments.
EmoEmph-Split v2 duration-ablation corpus: matched constrained and unconstrained phrases with blinded emotion, emphasis, and speaker-similarity ratings.
Compare constrained versus unconstrained adapters in the duration-ablation corpus using speaker-stratified emotion recognition, emphasis accuracy, and similarity MOS.
Duration ablation: constrained adapters scored 81% emotion, 94% emphasis, 4.1 similarity MOS; unconstrained scored 83%, 88%, 4.1.
Audit duration-ablation ratings by emotion and speaker, testing whether constraint-induced recognition losses concentrate in particular emotions or voices.
For five unseen speakers, constrained adapters yielded 72% emotion recognition and 3.6 similarity MOS versus 4.0 neutral.
Retain duration constraints for 94% emphasis accuracy, but defer broad deployment after five speakers fell below emotion and similarity targets.
Extend the duration-ablation plan with speaker-adaptive bounds; retest five failing voices for emotion, emphasis, and neutral-relative similarity.
Fit speaker-adaptive duration bounds from the ablation corpus, then resynthesize matched phrases for the five failing voices.
EmoEmph-Split v2 duration-ablation corpus adds speaker-adaptive resyntheses for five failing voices, paired with original ablation phrases.
Blind-rate ar3’s adaptive resyntheses against original phrases for five voices; compare emotion recognition, emphasis accuracy, and similarity MOS against neutral.
Adaptive bounds yielded 77% emotion recognition and 3.8 similarity MOS across five failing voices, still below 80% and neutral 4.0.
Reject adapter deployment despite 94% aggregate emphasis accuracy: five voices still miss emotion and similarity targets after speaker-adaptive bounds.
Use speaker-normalized prosody transport for phrase emotion, with pitch-range calibration and phoneme-local emphasis edits that preserve native timing.
Can speaker-normalized prosody transport restore emotion and similarity for the five failing voices while phoneme-local edits retain accurate emphasis?
For five failing voices, normalized prosody transport yields ≥80% emotion recognition, >90% emphasis accuracy, and speaker-similarity MOS ≥4.0.
Resynthesize EmoEmph-Split v2’s withheld combinations for five failing voices using normalized transport; blind-rate emotion, emphasis, and similarity versus neutral.
Five failing voices: normalized transport yielded 84% emotion recognition, 93% emphasis accuracy, and speaker-similarity MOS 4.1 versus neutral 4.0.
Advance normalized prosody transport to full unseen-speaker testing: the five previously failing voices now meet all three targets.
Train counterfactual-swap TTS with paired emotion-only and emphasis-only recordings, enforcing cycle consistency and speaker-identity reconstruction.
Can counterfactual swapping disentangle emotion and emphasis when paired recordings cover only a subset of combinations and speakers?
With 30% paired coverage, counterfactual-swap TTS reaches ≥80% emotion recognition, >90% emphasis accuracy, and similarity MOS ≥ neutral.
Train counterfactual-swap TTS with 30% paired coverage; blind-rate withheld EmoEmph-Split v2 combinations for emotion, emphasis, and neutral-relative similarity.
With 30% paired coverage, swap TTS scored 74% emotion recognition, 89% emphasis accuracy, and similarity MOS 3.8 versus neutral 4.0.
With 60% speaker-balanced paired coverage, swap TTS reaches ≥80% emotion recognition, >90% emphasis accuracy, and similarity MOS ≥ neutral.
Retrain swap TTS with 60% speaker-balanced pairs; blind-rate withheld combinations for emotion recognition, emphasis accuracy, and neutral-relative similarity MOS.
At 60% balanced coverage, swap TTS reached 81% emotion recognition, 92% emphasis accuracy, and similarity MOS 4.0 versus neutral 4.0.
Require 60% speaker-balanced pairing before adopting swap TTS; 30% coverage missed all targets, while 60% met them.

Emphasis placement accuracy exceeds 90%, with listener-rated speaker similarity no worse than neutral synthesis.
